commit 66fc13039422ba7df2d01a8ee0873e4ef965b50b (""mm: shmem_zero_setup
skip security check and lockdep conflict with XFS"") caused a regression
for SELinux by disabling any SELinux checking of mprotect PROT_EXEC on
shared anonymous mappings.  However
checking on such mprotect PROT_EXEC calls was inconsistent with the
checking on a mmap PROT_EXEC call for a shared anonymous mapping.  On a
mmap
column2: the security hook is passed a NULL file and knows it is dealing

column1: with an anonymous mapping and therefore applies an execmem check and no
file checks.  On a mprotect
column2: the security hook is passed a vma with a

column1: non-NULL vm_file (as this was set from the internally-created shmem
file during mmap) and therefore applies the file-based execute check
and no execmem check.  Since the aforementioned commit now marks the
shmem zero inode with the S_PRIVATE flag
and we have no checking at all on mprotect PROT_EXEC.  Add a test to
the mprotect hook logic for such private inodes
check in that case.  This makes the mmap and mprotect checking
consistent for shared anonymous mappings
ashmem.
